column1: # Every external source this pipeline reads, with the identifier it is pinned
# to. The fetching scripts read this file rather than holding URLs, so changing
# a source is a config change and shows up in a diff.
# checksum_source says who publishes the checksum being verified. "publisher"
# means the value is fetched from the publisher at run time and compared;
# "recorded_locally" means upstream publishes none and the stage records what
# it received instead of pretending to verify it. Nothing here is self-attested
# as a checksum baked into a script.
# A note on the two weight rows, because the licence question is the awkward
# part of this stage.
# ColabFold's own code is MIT. The AlphaFold2 parameters it downloads are a
# separate work under a separate licence, and which licence applies is not as
# simple as quoting the current README. The parameter file ColabFold fetches
# for this model type is the July 2021 archive, and that archive carries an
# embedded licence file whose text is the non-commercial, share-alike variant.
# The model's own repository now states that the parameters are licensed for
# any use with attribution, and its release notes describe that as a
# relicensing with no change to the parameters themselves. Both facts are
# recorded, the README states both, and 05_predict.sh writes the licence file
# it actually found inside the archive into results/environment/ so a reader
# can check rather than take either statement on trust.
